# AGENTS.md

Operational runbook for agents and harnesses working in this repo. Most runs start from a **Linear ticket** whose description is the task: read it, do it with the CLIs below, report back on the ticket. This file is about *operating* (which tool, which flags, what is safe), not about writing code.

## Operating Principles

1. **The ticket is the contract.** Do what the description and acceptance criteria say. If they are ambiguous or missing, comment on the ticket and stop; do not guess on anything outbound.
2. **Preview before you apply.** Anything that touches an external system (email, CRM, Linear, Slack) gets a dry run or a read-back first. For `gtm-attio` — which has no `--apply` and no dry-run — the `search` → write-once → read-back sequence **is** the mandatory preview, and the target email or domain must come from the ticket, never inferred.
3. **Reads are free, writes are deliberate.** Read as much as you need; make the smallest write that satisfies the ticket.
4. **Idempotent and resumable.** Re-run only failed items on a partial batch (target the failed ids/slugs), never the whole batch.
5. **Never leak secrets.** Do not print, log, commit, or paste API keys. See [Secrets](#secrets).
6. **Say what happened.** Report failures and skipped steps plainly on the ticket. Never claim success you did not verify.

## Picking Up a Linear Ticket

```bash
git branch --show-current                  # feature/* from Linear? keep it. Otherwise use agent/<topic>.
uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear issue EKK-1234 --json   # read the task (identifier or UUID)
uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear search "keyword" --json # find related tickets
```

1. Read the description, acceptance criteria, linked design artifacts, and comments.
2. If the ticket references `design/*` files, read them from `/Users/elvis/Documents/ai/design/`.
3. Move the issue to In Progress and leave a one-line "starting" comment (Linear MCP, see below; or `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear issue update/comment ... --apply` where MCP is unavailable — see `cli-linear-guide`).
4. Do the work using the [CLI Routing Table](#cli-routing-table).
5. Close out with the [Completion Protocol](#completion-protocol).

Linear access split:

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Auth check, list teams/issues, fetch one issue, search | `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear <viewer\|teams\|issues\|issue\|search> --json` (reads; the floor also guarantees filters, `--all`, and CLI writes) |
| Create/update issue, comment, change state | Linear MCP (default): `mcp__linear__save_issue`, `mcp__linear__save_comment` (see `linear-ticket-creator`); no MCP available: `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear issue create\|update\|comment ... --apply` (preview-first, see `cli-linear-guide`) |
| Oz cloud run needing SDK-level state transitions | `oz-linear-issue` skill |

`gtm-linear` is the PyPI package, **not** the npm `linear` CLI (`npx linear`). Do not diagnose with `which linear`. The CLI is read+write as of 0.4.0 (writes preview-first, gated by `--apply`); prefer `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear ...` so resolution can never fall back to a pre-CLI wheel (0.2.x installs no executable), and pin `--from 'gtm-linear==<version>'` when reproducibility matters. State transitions via the CLI take a workflow-state UUID (there is no states command) — resolve it with the SDK snippet in `cli-linear-ticket-from-branch`.

## CLI Routing Table

| Task | Tool | Entry point | Skill |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read Linear | gtm-linear | `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear <cmd> --json` | `cli-linear-guide` |
| Write Linear | Linear MCP (default) / gtm-linear CLI | `mcp__linear__*`; or `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear issue <create\|update\|comment> ... --apply` (preview-first) | `linear-ticket-creator`, `cli-linear-guide` |
| Personal email, Drive, Sheets, Calendar | gws | `gws <service> <resource> <method> --params '{...}'` | `cli-gws-personal-email`, `cli-gws-calendar-events` |
| System/automated email | Resend | Resend API | `cli-resend-guide`, `resend-system-email` |
| Attio CRM people/companies/notes | gtm-attio CLI | `uvx --from 'gtm-attio>=0.26.1' gtm-attio <people\|companies\|notes> ...` (see note) | `cli-attio-guide` |
| Apollo enrichment, Parallel/Exa web search | gtm-sdk CLI | `uv run python -m cli.main <apollo\|parallel\|exa> ...` | `cli-gtm-guide`, `parallel-web-search` |
| Gmail URL → API id | gtm-sdk CLI | `uv run python -m cli.main gmail url decode "<url>"` | `cli-gws-personal-email` |
| Granola meeting export | gtm-sdk CLI | `uv run python -m cli.main granola ...` | `cli-gtm-guide` |
| Secrets | Infisical | `infisical run --env=<env> -- <cmd>` | `cli-infisical-guide` |
| Ad-hoc data queries | duckdb / xan | `duckdb db -c "SQL"`, `xan from -f json in.json -o out.csv` | `duckdb-cli-guide`, `convert-tabular-data` |
| Lint / type check | trunk | `trunk check --all` | `trunk-cli-guide` |
| Task tracking | beads | `bd ready`, `bd show`, `bd update --claim`, `bd close` | `cli-beads-guide` |

**Attio note:** Attio record operations (people, companies, notes) run through the standalone `gtm-attio` CLI — `uvx --from 'gtm-attio>=0.26.1' gtm-attio <people|companies|notes> ...` (0.26.1, 2026-10-09, closed [sdk-python-attio#35](https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio/issues/35); 0.26.0 and earlier wheels install no executable; see the `cli-attio-guide` skill; pin `--from 'gtm-attio==<version>'` when reproducibility matters). It works from any directory — including Oz cloud runs, where it is the only Attio CLI — and needs only `ATTIO_API_KEY` (process env, or `.env`/`.env.local` in the cwd). **Writes apply immediately — there is no `--apply` and no dry-run:** resolve the target with `search` (or `notes list`) first, write once, then read the record back and check the envelope. Single-record people/company/note operations → `gtm-attio`; batch writes → `accounts batch-add-people` / `batch-add-companies` on the gtm-sdk CLI with `--apply` (see `cli-gtm-guide`). The `cli.main attio` group inside a `gtm-sdk/` checkout still exists (Modal-backed, richer search filters) but is not the default path. Attio MCP tools (`mcp__attio__*`) remain acceptable for ad-hoc reads.

For any request that mentions Attio or CRM sync, route first: record operations (people, companies, notes) → the `cli-attio-guide` skill (`uvx --from 'gtm-attio>=0.26.1' gtm-attio`); LinkedIn-to-Attio pipeline work → the `crm-pipeline-management` skill.

### CLI contract (gtm-sdk and gtm-attio CLIs)

- Success data is JSON on stdout. gtm-sdk CLI errors go to stderr; `gtm-attio` prints every envelope — failures included — to stdout and signals via exit code (`0` success/partial success, `1` runtime failure, `2` usage error).
- **gtm-sdk mutating commands are `--apply`-gated** (`accounts batch-*`, `attio companies`, `attio enrichment`) — without `--apply` they are previews; run once without, inspect the output, then re-run with it. Exception: in-repo `attio people`/`attio notes` and every `gtm-attio` write apply **immediately** — no `--apply`, no dry-run; preview-first means resolving the target with `search` (or `notes list`), writing once, then reading the record back.
- Attio commands return `success`, `partial_success`, `action` (`created|updated|searched|listed|noop|failed`), `warnings`, `errors`. Treat `partial_success: true` or non-empty `errors` as a failure to report, not a pass.

### Email routing

> **MANDATORY: before any email task, read [`cli-gws-personal-email`](skills/cli-gws-personal-email/SKILL.md) in full.** This applies to every send, reply, draft, or thread lookup, including replies to archived mail found with msgvault. Do not rely on memory or the summary below. The skill covers the send-as alias check, the 404 limits on other mailboxes, the threading limits, and non-ASCII header encoding. Skipping it has caused a garbled subject line and an unthreaded reply.

- **gws (Gmail)**: message is from you personally, relationship/thread continuity matters, one-off or small hand-managed batch. Plain text only (no HTML, no hyperlinks, no auto-signature).
- **gws sender identities**: the agent may send as either `elvis@elvis.ai` or `ekk0809@gmail.com` (configured as a send-as alias, so both go out through the same `gws` auth). Pick the From address that matches the ticket or the existing thread (reply from the address the thread was sent to); if the ticket names neither and there is no thread, default to `elvis@elvis.ai`. Set it explicitly with the From header rather than relying on the account default, and say which address was used in the ticket comment.
- **Resend**: message is from the system/product, automated, templated, scheduled, or higher-volume.
- Uncertain: personal one-off → gws; system-triggered → Resend.
- **Never send email on a ticket's behalf unless the ticket explicitly says to send.** Otherwise create a draft and put the draft text/ID in the ticket comment.

## Secrets

- Required keys by tool: `LINEAR_API_KEY` (`lin_api_...`), `ATTIO_API_KEY`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, Modal tokens, Infisical machine identity. `gws` uses its own OAuth config (`gws auth status` to check).
- In Oz cloud runs, the Team-scoped secrets are already in the environment. Use them as-is; if one is missing, report "secret unavailable" on the ticket. Do not read another secret store (1Password etc.) to work around it.
- Locally, inject with `infisical run --env=<env> -- <command>`.
- Never run `infisical secrets` (list/get) in a way that prints values. Filter to names only (`| cut -d= -f1`).
- Never echo env vars, `cat .env`, or include keys in commit messages, ticket comments, or files.

## Completion Protocol

Run before marking anything done.

1. **Verify the result, not the command.** Re-read the changed state (e.g. `search --email` after an Attio upsert, `gws gmail ... get` after a send, `uvx --from 'gtm-linear>=0.4.0' gtm-linear issue <ID> --json` after a transition). Use the `verification-before-completion` skill.
2. **Comment on the ticket** (Linear MCP `save_comment`): what was done, counts, links (PR, record URLs, run URLs), and anything skipped or failed. Keep it short and factual. Check existing comments first so you do not post a duplicate.
3. **Transition state:**
   - Fully done and verified → Done (`type == completed`).
   - Partial or blocked → leave In Progress; comment what remains, why, and the next action.
   - Invalid or unnecessary → Canceled with an explanation.
   - If the target state cannot be resolved unambiguously, leave the issue unchanged and say so.
4. **File follow-ups** for remaining work as new Linear tickets (`linear-ticket-creator`) and link them.
5. Never claim success when an update or its verification failed. Do not blindly retry a mutation that may have succeeded.

## Git, Branches, and Pushing

- **Branches:** agent-created branches use `agent/<topic>`. If a Linear ticket pre-created a `feature/*` branch, keep that name (Linear's linkage depends on it). Never use `claude/` or other provider prefixes. Isolate multi-file refactors on their own branch.
- **Commits:** credit only human authors. Never add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers (Claude, Oz, or any AI) to commits or PR descriptions. Commit messages lead with WHY (the problem/motivation); the diff shows the what.
- **Push policy:**
  - Never push without a clean `roborev review --wait` on HEAD. `--wait` is mandatory; a bare enqueue is not a pass (block with `roborev wait`). If roborev fails to run, say so and ask.
  - `agent/*`, `feature/*`, `conductor/*`: after the roborev gate, `git pull --rebase && git push` is fine.
  - `main`, `master`, release/protected, or unsure: stop after the local commit, say what would be pushed, and ask.
  - Never force-push without an explicit ask. If a push fails, surface the error and ask; do not loop or rewrite history.
- **Git hooks:** this repo deliberately has no Trunk git-hook actions (they
  collide with the Entire CLI's hook chain and block commits/pushes; see
  `actions.disabled` in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`). Hooks run from the dispatcher
  installed by `.trunk/hooks/install-ai-hooks.sh`: Entire session tracking +
  AI co-author stripping + branch-prefix policy + git-lfs hooks, with policy
  in the tracked `.trunk/hooks/chain-*.sh`. Run the installer once per
  machine/checkout; verify with `.trunk/hooks/install-ai-hooks.sh --check`.
  If a `trunk check` run from an old checkout re-points `core.hooksPath` at a
  trunk cache dir, re-run the installer (or `git config core.hooksPath
  ~/.config/git/ai-hooks`). The gates are covered by
  `.trunk/hooks/test-chain-hooks.sh`; run it when touching the chain scripts.
  Note: local pushes no longer run `trunk check` — run `trunk check --all`
  before pushing, per [Session End](#session-end); PRs are covered by unit
  tests and pullfrog review.
- **Conductor workspaces:** edit inside the workspace, never the primary repo path.
- **Merging PRs:** no merge queue is configured for this repo (`SanhedrinTech/ai`) — `trunk merge` fails here ("Merge queue does not exist for your repo"). The human merges via the Conductor PR view or GitHub (UI or `gh pr merge`); agents never merge a PR without an explicit ask.

## Where Things Live

- **`gtm-sdk/`** is a separate, gitignored git repo (`elviskahoro/gtm-sdk`), editable-installed. All of `cli/`, `src/`, `libs/` live there; GTM infrastructure changes are made and committed *in `gtm-sdk/`*, not `ai/`. Fresh clone: `git clone git@github.com:elviskahoro/gtm-sdk.git` inside `ai/`, then `uv sync`.
- **`projects/`**: self-contained experiments in `ai/`.
- **`skills/`**: one folder per skill; descriptions auto-load. Run `skill-finder` to discover one. Skills use plain kebab-case names. Skills always get written in `/Users/elvis/Documents/ai/`, never inside a worktree.
- **`design/`**: design artifacts, see below.
- **`tmp/`**: all scratch and intermediate files. Gitignored. Never write scratch files to the repo root or beside source.

### Design artifacts

Everything goes to `/Users/elvis/Documents/ai/design/` (absolute path, even from a worktree or `projects/*`). Never create another `design/` directory. Name: `status-YYYYMMDDHHMM-objective_details-<type>-NN.md`.

- Status prefix: `backlog-` (default for new), `done-` (completed/merged), `cancelled-` (abandoned).
- Types: `spec`, `plan`, `findings`, `ticket`, `prompt` (no `-NN`), `todo` (`.py`, no `-NN`).
- Numbering starts at `-01`; edit in place while in scope; increment only for out-of-scope follow-ups.
- A `ticket` artifact flips to `done-` as soon as its Linear ticket is filed, not when the work ships.
- Use `design-artifact-naming` for the details. Do not create loose summary/investigation `.md` files; report in the ticket comment instead.

## Running Python and Scripts

- Package management is `uv` only: `uv sync`, `uv run <cmd>`, `uv pip install`. Never bare `pip`/`pip3`.
- Scripts that touch files beside themselves anchor on `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`, not the cwd (`uv run path/to/script.py` does not change directory).
- For tabular data use `xan`; for DuckDB use the `duckdb` CLI, not Python wrappers.
- Testing on Oz: use cloud runs, not local: `oz agent run-cloud --environment <ENV_ID> --prompt "..."` (see `oz-platform`; the CLI was renamed from `oz-preview` to `oz`).

## Reading External Docs

Try `llms.txt` first, then the `.md` variant of the URL, then `raw.githubusercontent.com/...`, then the repo's `/docs` or `/examples`. If a URL 404s, search for the current location instead of guessing. Cross-host redirects often fail and long pages truncate around 150k characters.

## Issue Tracking (beads)

Use `bd` for local task tracking, not markdown TODO lists. `bd ready`, `bd show <id>`, `bd update <id> --claim`, `bd close <id>`. Dependencies use `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>`. Run `bd prime` for the full command reference. Linear is the system of record for ticket-driven work; beads is for your own working breakdown.

## Session End

1. File follow-ups (Linear for shared work, `bd` for local).
2. Run quality gates if code changed (`trunk check --all`).
3. Complete the [Completion Protocol](#completion-protocol).
4. Commit locally; push only per the [push policy](#git-branches-and-pushing).
5. Hand off: final ticket comment plus a short summary with links.

# Attio SDK Python

## Beads Issue Tracking

- This repository uses Beads with the DoltHub remote `elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio`.
- Use `bd prime` for the current workflow context, `bd ready` to find unblocked work, and `bd create`/`bd update`/`bd close` for issue changes.
- Pull remote changes explicitly with `bd dolt pull`; push committed Dolt changes with `bd dolt push`.
- Authenticate locally with `DOLT_REMOTE_USER` and `DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD`; never commit credentials or `.beads` runtime/database files.

## Git Workflow

- Commits are allowed when the user explicitly asks to commit
- Always show the user what will be committed before committing
- Do NOT push to remote unless explicitly asked

## Landing PRs

PRs land through the Trunk Merge Queue, not the GitHub Merge button.

- Submit: `trunk merge <pr-number>` (a number, not a URL or branch name).
- Check once: `trunk merge status <pr-number>`. States: Queued, Testing,
  Tests Passed, Merged. Report the state and stop. Never poll in a loop.
- Never use `gh pr merge` or the GitHub Merge button. They bypass the queue.
- Never use `--force`, `pause` or `resume`.
- Leave priority at the default (`medium`). `urgent` and `high` are for
  incidents and need an explicit reason from the user.
- Failed or PENDING_FAILURE: PENDING_FAILURE may be a flake, so retry once.
  Failed means push a fix to the PR branch and resubmit. Do not resubmit
  blindly in a loop.
- Auth failure: run `trunk login` once and retry.
- Refuse to queue from main or a protected branch.
- A `Closes #N` line in the PR body auto-closes the issue when the queue lands
  the PR. Do not close the issue by hand beforehand.

## SDK Update Guide

This SDK is generated using Speakeasy from an OpenAPI spec.

### Key Files

- **SDK Generator**: Speakeasy (https://www.speakeasy.com/)
- **OpenAPI specs**: stored in `openapi/` directory, named `api-YYYYMMDDHHMM.json`
- **Overlay**: `overlay.yaml` applies targeted fixes to the spec before generation (timestamp format fixes, `list` → `list_id` parameter renames)
- **Workflow config**: `.speakeasy/workflow.yaml` defines the generation pipeline
- **Generation config**: `.speakeasy/gen.yaml` has Speakeasy settings (Python target, async mode, package name, etc.)

### Update Steps

1. **Check for updates first** — this fetches the latest spec, diffs it
   against the current one, and verifies overlay health in one shot:

   ```bash
   uv run python ci/pipeline.py check-openapi
   ```

   Exit 0 means nothing to do. Exit 1 prints a report of structural drift
   (new/removed/changed operations, schema changes) and/or overlay problems.
   It never touches `openapi/` — the fetched spec lands in `tmp/` and is
   deleted. Add `--report PATH` for a JSON report, `--no-strict` to always
   exit 0. `ci/spec_diff.py` also has standalone `diff OLD NEW` and
   `check-overlay` subcommands.

   The scheduled `.github/workflows/spec-update-check.yml` workflow runs this
   check weekly (Mondays 09:00 UTC). On drift it regenerates, runs pytest,
   and opens a PR (needs the `SPEAKEASY_API_KEY` repo secret); without the
   secret it opens an issue with the report instead. It replaces the old
   daily `Generate` workflow (sdk_generation.yaml), which fetched and
   regenerated blindly every day regardless of drift — the weekly check is
   now the only automated regeneration path. Generation itself refuses to
   run while the overlay is unhealthy (`_verify_overlay_health`), so a
   manual `generate` is gated the same way as the workflow.

2. **Fetch the latest spec** (when the check reports drift):

   ```bash
   uv run python ci/pipeline.py fetch-openapi
   ```

   This downloads from `https://api.attio.com/openapi/api`, saves it with a
   timestamp, and updates `workflow.yaml`.

3. **Verify the overlay still applies cleanly**:

   ```bash
   uv run python ci/spec_diff.py check-overlay
   ```

   This catches three silent failure modes: dead targets (JSONPath matches
   nothing — speakeasy silently skips the action, so a fix you think is
   applied is not), uncovered timestamp values (`format: date` value nodes
   with no *live* `.format` removal action, which regenerate as `date`
   instead of `str`), and error-code enums out of sync (a hardcoded overlay
   enum that drops a value the spec's `anyOf` union gained). Historical
   examples: the `POST/PUT /v2/objects/{object}/records` 400 `.code.enum`
   targets died when Attio moved error codes to `anyOf` unions; all
   `/v2/activities/{activity}/records*` endpoints shipped with `date`-typed
   timestamps before they got overlay entries.

4. **Update the overlay if needed**. If `oneOf` indices shifted, endpoints
   were added, or error schemas changed shape, update `overlay.yaml`
   accordingly, then re-run `check-overlay` until it is healthy.

5. **Run Speakeasy generation**:

   ```bash
   uv run python ci/pipeline.py generate --no-fetch
   ```

   This runs `speakeasy run` (host CLI when authenticated via login, or when
   `SPEAKEASY_USE_HOST_CLI` + `SPEAKEASY_API_KEY` are set — the scheduled
   workflow's path; pinned Dagger container otherwise), then re-applies
   `ci/post_generate_patch.py` (manual patches `overlay.yaml` cannot
   express, e.g. the GET /v2/self `active` value discriminators in
   `src/attio/models/get_v2_selfop.py`, the `scripts/publish.sh` and
   `scripts/release.sh` wrappers, the standalone CLI entry point/docs in
   `pyproject.toml` and `README.md`, and SDKHooks `init_hooks` wiring plus
   the hooks-package re-export in `src/attio/_hooks/sdkhooks.py` and
   `src/attio/_hooks/__init__.py`). Drop `--no-fetch` to also
   adopt a freshly fetched spec. Note the Dagger path exports only `src/`
   back to the host — docs/, README, pyproject and USAGE refresh on the
   host-CLI path (the default) — and it logs that when chosen.

6. **Review generated changes**:
   - Check `git diff` for new/modified SDK methods in `src/attio/`
   - Verify new models in `src/attio/models/`
   - Check for any type errors: `uv run mypy src/`
   - Run tests: `uv run pytest -q`
   - Ensure the package still builds: `uv build`
   - Confirm `pyproject.toml`'s dev group still contains `dagger-io`,
     `pytest`, `pytest-asyncio` — speakeasy rewrites `pyproject.toml` from
     `.speakeasy/gen.yaml`, and they only survive because they are declared
     in `gen.yaml` `python.additionalDependencies.dev`. If they vanish,
     restore them and run `uv lock && uv sync`.

7. **Verify the version** in `.speakeasy/gen.yaml` (`python.version`) matches
   `pyproject.toml` and `src/attio/_version.py` (speakeasy auto-bumps the
   patch version on each regeneration with changes).

### Important Notes

- The SDK is fully generated code — manual edits to `src/attio/` will be overwritten on next generation.
- The overlay exists because Speakeasy infers `date` type from ISO8601 timestamp strings, but Attio returns timestamps as strings that should stay as `str` in Python.
- The `list` → `list_id` renames avoid shadowing Python's built-in `list`.
- Description-only spec changes (marketing copy) are reported by `check-openapi` but do not count as structural drift, so they do not trigger the automated workflow.

- `.trunk/trunk.yaml`: plugin catalog bumped to v1.11.0 with new plugin sources (oss-linter-trunk-config, pyrefly, add-trailing-comma), a kjanat/actionlint v1.17.0 download override, the reference's linter version bumps, pinact/buildifier enabled, inline-commented deviations (yamllint `comments` rule disabled, vale/tach omitted, generated-code exclusions extended to pyrefly/add-trailing-comma), and the merge queue's `required_statuses` renamed to the real bare job check-run names ("Lint with Trunk", "pytest").
- `trunk-check.yml`: the lint job renamed to `Lint with Trunk` so its check-run name matches the gate; step names collapsed.
- All workflow actions now SHA-pinned with version comments (pinact), including `pypi.yml`'s `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` moving from the branch-pinned `release/v1` to the v1.14.2 release commit.
- `ci/release.sh` (shfmt tabs) and `ci/post_generate_patch.py` (generator reflow) reformatted under the new fmt versions.
- New plugin symlinks under `.trunk/plugins/` (including one for tach, which is not adopted).

Verified live against the repo: PR 43's check runs are indeed posted under bare job names (`pytest`, `lint`, plus the separate `Trunk Check` annotation side-channel), so the `required_statuses` rename matches how GitHub actually posts Actions job check runs — the previous "Trunk Check / lint" / "Tests / pytest" names would have deadlocked the queue. The kjanat/actionlint v1.17.0 download URLs resolve (HTTP 200 for the linux/darwin assets with the expected naming), so the override is valid.

## Issues

**Low — `.trunk/trunk.yaml:278`: stale required-status name left in the actions comment.**
The commit renames the merge queue gate from "Trunk Check / lint" to "Lint with Trunk", but the comment in the `actions.disabled` section (immediately adjacent to the `disabled` list this commit edits) still reads `# trunk-check-pre-push is redundant with roborev + the merge queue's # required "Trunk Check / lint" status.` Anyone re-verifying gate wiring from that comment will look for a status that no longer exists. Fix: update the comment to "Lint with Trunk" in the same pass.

**Low — `.github/workflows/spec-update-check.yml:25-26`: stale gate names in a file this commit touches.**
The comment explaining why GITHUB_TOKEN-opened PRs bypass the gates still references `the required "Trunk Check / lint" and "Tests / pytest" gates (merge.required_statuses in .trunk/trunk.yaml)`. The commit edits this file (pinact pinning) while renaming both statuses, so the cross-reference it maintains is now wrong: a future maintainer re-checking `merge.required_statuses` from this comment will not find either named status. Fix: update the comment to "Lint with Trunk" and "pytest".

**Low — `.trunk/plugins/tach-plugin`: dead symlink for a plugin that is deliberately not adopted.**
The new symlink points into `~/.cache/trunk/plugins/.../oss-linter-trunk-tach/...`, but `trunk.yaml` declares no `tach-plugin` source and the commit explicitly documents tach as omitted (no `tach.toml` in this repo). Unlike the `pyrefly`/`add-trailing-comma` symlinks, which correspond to newly declared sources, this one is a leftover from local experimentation with the reference config: it references a machine-local cache path, is broken on every other checkout and on CI, and suggests to readers that tach is wired up when it is not. Fix: delete `.trunk/plugins/tach-plugin` from the commit.

The two-line header (`# This file controls the behavior of Trunk: https://docs.trunk.io/cli` / `# To learn more about the format of this file, see ...`) was collapsed by the new fmt stack into a single line: `...trunk.io/cli # To learn more about the format of this file, see https://docs.trunk.io/reference/trunk-yaml`.
